hook: A very short file about a young cockatoo that thinks and writes like a six-to-eight-year-old human. There is no violence here; the weight comes from a few scrawled notes whose misspellings the file keeps intact on purpose. Read it slowly, and let the small details in the description register before you reach the log.
whyItMatters: SCP-1192 shows how little an SCP article needs in order to land: one short exchange, one researcher note, and a handful of childish lines. The anomaly is not a threat to anyone but a situation someone is trapped in, and the clinical format makes that harder, not easier, to look away from. It is a good pick for readers who want something that lingers rather than shocks.
thingsToNotice:
The physical details are clues: a bird that will not eat seeds, cannot preen, can barely fly, and has a healed bruise on the back of its head, all consistent with a child who does not know how to live in this body. The bird calls itself Timmi and writes down a Montana address, yet agents find a seven-year-old named Timothy living there with his parents, and nothing about that family seems wrong. The file never explains who or what is in that house, and that unanswered question is the real horror.

The researcher note then lists the drawings so each one cuts deeper: race cars and monsters, the question of why he is a bird, a child with two adults scratched out and torn, and finally a page covered in 'mom' and 'home'. The detail that he asked for video games he physically cannot play is easy to skim past and hard to forget.
